conclusion: CRC-32C detects record and chunk corruption, while SHA-256 is the whole-image identity; neither checksum can replace the other's validation scope.
decision: Validate the copied-byte CRC before mutating staging and recompute SHA-256 over exactly the declared image bytes before publishing an immutable object.
invalidated_assumptions: A valid per-chunk CRC is sufficient to establish whole-image identity or complete upload order.
observation: Runtime matrices exercise CRC/SHA failure paths and the protocol explicitly separates copied-chunk corruption detection from final image digest binding.
question_or_symptom: Why must an A1 implementation retain both per-chunk CRC-32C and a final whole-image SHA-256?
